chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Hammad ibn ʿUthman, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAli al-Halabi; and al-Husayn ibn Saʿid, from ʿAli ibn al-Nuʿman and Muhammad ibn Sinan and ʿAbd Allah ibn Miskan, from Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Halabi, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, that the two of them asked him about one who recites بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ when he wants to recite Fatihat al-Kitab, and he said:
He may recite it for them, if he wishes, quietly, and if he wishes, aloud.
He said: Then does he recite it with the other surah? He said: No.

Thus, the proper way to understand this report is what we stated regarding the first report, namely interpreting it in light of taqiyyah. It is also possible that what is meant is one who is in a supererogatory salat and wishes to recite part of a surah; in that case it is permissible for him not to recite بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ. This clarifies what we have mentioned.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Dissimulation for protection under constrained circumstances.
key_terms.بِبِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ: The basmalah recited before a surah in salat.
key_terms.جَهْرًا: Recitation aloud in an audible manner.
key_terms.سُورَةٍ: A chapter, or part of a chapter, of the Qur'an.
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: The opening chapter of the Qur'an, recited in prayer.

ai.seo_question: Is it necessary to recite بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ before the second surah in salat?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of reciting بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ in salat, especially before al-Fatihah and another surah. The compiler explains that the narration is to be understood either as issued under taqiyyah or as referring to a nafilah prayer in which only part of a surah is recited.
